intro: Woodside is a town on the San Francisco Peninsula, and its hills run up to Skyline Boulevard, where a coast redwood called the Methuselah Tree stands. A reader calls it nearly two thousand years old and forty-four feet around, and says it is easy to reach from the road. They sent a photograph of its furrowed, burled and hollowed trunk, and the Peninsula Open Space Trust has written about it.

trees.name: The Methuselah Tree

location.address: Skyline Boulevard, San Mateo County, California

trees.story:
"This is the Methuselah tree, a local landmark on the San Francisco Bay peninsula," a reader wrote. "Nearly 2,000 years old, 44 feet around. Easily accessible from Skyline Boulevard." Their photograph shows the base, a vast reddish trunk with deeply furrowed bark, burls and a dark hollow, rising out of green redwood sprays.

The reader linked a Peninsula Open Space Trust article on old-growth redwood, which we could not open, so the figures here are theirs. Forty-four feet is about 13.4 metres. A coast redwood that wide and close to two thousand years old would be among the old survivors of a forest that was almost entirely logged in the nineteenth century, which is why a single trunk like this gets its own name.

The tree stands near Skyline Boulevard, and the reader says it is easy to reach from the road. A fence at the edge of the frame suggests a viewing path, but we do not know where exactly to park, so check the trust's own guidance before you go. If you have visited, tell us on this page how you reached it.
